qs.q: Gynecomastia in a patient with liver cirrhosis occurs because of
o: Direct oestrogen secretion by hepatocellular carcinoma cells
Increased androgen production stimulating breast ductal growth
Impaired hepatic metabolism of oestrogens causing relative excess
Portal hypertension causing direct hormonal effects on breast tissue
qs.e: Cirrhosis impairs hepatic oestrogen metabolism, leading to relative oestrogen excess over androgens. This oestrogen-androgen imbalance drives ductal proliferation causing gynecomastia.

qs.q: A patient with liver cirrhosis and portal hypertension may experience ascites due to:
o: Decreased capillary hydrostatic pressure in the peritoneal cavity.
Increased plasma albumin synthesis by the liver.
Excessive absorption of fluid from the peritoneal cavity.
Increased capillary hydrostatic pressure and decreased plasma oncotic pressure.
qs.e: Ascites (fluid accumulation in the peritoneal cavity) in liver cirrhosis is primarily caused by two factors: increased capillary hydrostatic pressure due to portal hypertension, which pushes fluid out of the splanchnic circulation, and decreased plasma oncotic pressure due to impaired albumin synthesis by the diseased liver, which reduces the osmotic pull of fluid back into the capillaries.
